Unlike routine rank computations, the count depends on the full Jordan partition and its global multiplicative scalar symmetries, and the calculation uses the radical quotient of finite module endomorphism rings plus cyclic return-map restrictions. The result has distinct existence, exact counting, and probability consequences without claiming an extension to nonsplit or singular operators.
